name: BSE Ltd.
business_summary: Asia's oldest stock exchange and listed exchange operator: equity cash, Sensex/Bankex/Sensex50 index options and futures, currency and commodity-derivatives, mutual-fund distribution platform (StAR MF), listings, data and index licensing. Debt-free, operating margin 67%. Q2 FY27 PAT ~Rs809cr (+45% y/y; screener Rs773cr, -7% q/q), revenue +34%. Mcap Rs1.56 lakh cr, P/E 53x, stock +53% in 12 months and +15.5% in 1 month. Stock moves with SEBI derivatives policy (closing auction session, expiry and settlement rules), NSE competition (NSE listed on 2026-09-21), and retail trading activity.

revenue_mix.segment: cash market, MF platform, listing, data, services

exposures.mechanism: +20% traded value/ demat additions: transaction charges ~70% of revenue (equity derivatives dominate; model knowledge) => revenue +14% = ~Rs800cr on TTM Rs5,444cr; incremental margin ~90% => EBITDA +Rs680cr = +19% on TTM EBITDA Rs3,576cr; EV/MCap ~0.97 (debt-free); persistence 0.5 => +9.

evidence.note: Q2 PAT +45% y/y to Rs809cr, revenue +34%, -7% q/q; derivatives recovery signalled (ET/Reuters/CNBC TV18)

exposures.mechanism: One tightening step (e.g., fewer weekly expiries, higher contract size, settlement changes) cuts derivatives volumes ~10% => revenue -7%, EBITDA -10%; persistence 0.75; plus multiple compression at P/E 53x => -8; SEBI is reviewing CAS/ F&O settlement after the chaotic August rollout (Bloomberg 2026-09-03).

evidence.note: SEBI panel view on CAS; settlement may move to last-30-minute VWAP; BSE +2.8% (NiftyTrader 2026-10-15; Moneycontrol 2026-10-06)
SEBI to review F&O settlement methodology after CAS (NDTV Profit)

exposures.mechanism: STT/transaction tax hikes on options raise trader cost and cut turnover: +1 step => volumes -8% => EBITDA -9% x 0.75 persistence => -6 (model knowledge: option STT raised in 2024; later changes unverified).

BSE's Sensex/Bankex options share of premium turnover (about 15-20%, model knowledge) vs NSE: +5pp share lifts derivatives revenue ~25% => EBITDA +30%, persistence 0.5 => +12 (hypothetical SSU defined for NSE-BSE market share); NSE IPO (listed 2026-09-21 at Rs1,800) strengthens its competitive spending but BSE CEO ruled out NSE self-listing issue (3 Sep) and brokers are the swing factor.

+10% monthly SIP + DII inflows lifts cash volumes, StAR MF platform order flow (mutual-fund units distribution is a growing BSE revenue line), and listing/index licences; revenue +3% => EBITDA +4% x 0.75 => +3.5.
FIIs 17.1% (21.3% in June): FPI flows lift cash and derivatives volumes (BSE beta 1.3-1.6 to Nifty): +3.
Volatility lifts options turnover and premiums (positive) but risk-off cuts retail participation; ambiguous; +1.0.
Empirical -5.88 (t=-1.9): high-multiple (53x) stock; a +25bp Fed hike compresses; shrunk to -3 as the rate-duration effect is generic.
Structural shift of household savings into markets raises demat accounts and active traders; +1 => 5% revenue CAGR lift persistent => +4.

supply_chain.counterparty: Brokers (Groww, Zerodha, Angel One etc.) and HFT/prop firms
supply_chain.note: retail and prop order flow; Groww is a top-3 broker

recent_developments: 2026-08: SEBI closing auction session (CAS) rollout chaotic; BSE rose as options settlement under review (2026-09-03/04 +5%)
2026-09-21: NSE IPO lists on BSE/NSE at Rs1,800; 2026-09-24 BSE -1% on muted debut

key_risks: SEBI derivatives curbs (expiry days, contract size, STT)
NSE competitive response after its IPO
Sequential revenue decline; high expectations at 53x P/E
Market-share concentration in a few products (Sensex options)
upside_triggers: Favourable CAS/settlement outcome keeping expiry-day volumes
BSE market-share gains in index options
Retail participation revival with rising markets
